title: Pre-registration of stage E16: the one-constant population control (L-SHADE 6D vs 18D) on the five engineering problems
status: requested by peer review (Stage 3, roadmap item REV-09); exploratory relative to the confirmatory CEC2014 analysis; reported whatever it shows

design.arm_definition: stock L-SHADE port (published settings: H=6, archive 2.6N, p=0.11, LPSR to N_min=4) with only N_init changed: round(6D) vs round(18D)
design.constraint_handling: Deb's feasibility rule, equality tolerance 1e-4, as in Section 7
design.seeds: deterministic hash of (suite, func, dim, algorithm, tag, run) with tag E16_engpop_<problem>; independent of the E5 runs

per_problem: feasibility of each arm and Fisher's exact two-sided test
Cliff's delta between the arms on the Deb-rule fitness the runs minimise (negative favours 6D), 95% percentile bootstrap over runs (20,000 resamples, seed 20261002)
two-sided Mann-Whitney U test, Holm-corrected across the five problems
best and median objective among feasible runs
analysis.verdict_rule: 6D better / 18D better when the interval excludes 0 in that direction AND p_Holm<0.05; negligible when the interval lies inside |delta|<0.147; otherwise no detectable difference

directional_expectation: If the population result is about evaluations per variable, 6D should not be worse than 18D on the problem with the fewest evaluations per variable (RC06, D=38, ~395 per variable), and 18D should not be worse on the problems with the most (pressure vessel and gear train, D=4, 3,750 per variable). Either failure is reported as evidence against the budget-per-variable reading.
commitments: Reported in the paper whatever it shows.
Nothing in E16 may change the frozen configuration or any earlier result.
